questions.subject: General English
questions.questionText: Sl: In a typical Indian village today, one is certain to find groups of women talking about finance. In a society where women play significant but never-recognised roles, being a part of an SHG which gives them such financial power is indeed a matter of pride. P Sitting there, they might proudly introduce themselves by saying that they are members of a self- help group (SHG). Altematively, they might lend money at reasonable interest rates to members for starting small businesses. They can be seen sitting under a tree, in an abandoned school building, or in the front yard of a village resident's dilapidated home, holding thick notebooks. S : An SHG is usually a community group of 10-12 women from similar socio-economic back- ground who pool their financial resources for taking up joint economic activities.

questions.subject: General English
questions.questionText: The first American settlers happened to live in the midst of perhaps the most exciting period in the history of the English language. Had the settlers gone a quarter of a century earlier, America might well have preserved those pre- vious forms, as it preserved many other archaisms. P • Similarly, thee and thou pronoun forms were also dying out. This was a time when 12,000 words were being added to the language. One such change which these first settlers had already adopted was to use the s form on verbs, saying has rather than hath, runs rather than runneth. S • It was also a time of considerable change in the structure of the language.

questions.questionText: Sl: In 1984, two small clay tablets of vaguely rectangular shape were found in Tell Brak, Syria, dating from the fourth millennium BCE. One of the animals may have been a goat, in which case, the other probably was a sheep. S : These two tablets were seen by an expert the year before the Gulf War, in an unostentatious display case in the Archaeological Museum of Baghdad.

questions.questionText: Sl: For generations, the Balaraju pond remained the primary water source of Perakalapudi village in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh. S6 : It was only after major restoration work was carried out to restore the pond's storage capacity that the community could return to its traditional livelihood. By the 2000s, decades of water mismanagement led to a rapid drop in the groundwater table as well. However, overexploitation caused the pond to shrink to half its original size and reduced its water storage capacity by 60 per cent. The pond, spread across 24 hec- tares, supported irigation, sus- tained the fishing community, met household needs and remained home to a wide variety of flora and fauna. S • As the pond disappeared, the households relied on groundwater to meet their daily needs.

questions.subject: General English
questions.questionText: Sl: Circadian rhythm is a term used to refer to the physical, mental and behavioural changes an organism experiences over a 24-hour cycle. S6: Maintaining a good circadian rhythm through appropriate expo- sure to natural light, consistent sleep schedules and times of eating, and adequate physical exercise during the day can allow an organism to live a healthy life. P : Prolonged disruption, moreover, can cause long-term damages such as metabolic diseases, cardio- vascular problems, and mental health issues. questions.questionText: Sl : Drought is a continuous and lengthy period during which no significant rainfall is recorded during the rainy season. questions.questionText: Sl : Drought is a continuous and lengthy period during which no significant rainfall is recorded during the rainy season. S6: In India, droughts are more frequent in the areas where the average annual rainfall is less than 60 cm and the variability of rainfall is over 20 per cent. P • This definition however, does not apply to Mawsynram and Cherra- punji, where even one week recording less than 0•25 mm of rainfall may be considered as a drought period. In general, the areas recording less than 60 cm of rainfall annually and in which the variability of rainfall is more than 20 per cent are the drought prone areas in India In India, the Meteorological Department has defined drought as a period of at least 22 con- secutive days on none of which is there more than 025 mm of rainfall. Areas where the variability of rainfall varies between 20 to 60 per cent are the chronic drought prone areas.

I have implied that there are a number Of things at stake—changes in goals, skills, philosophy or beliefs, behaviour, etc. Subjectively these different aspects are experienced in a diffuse, incoherent manner. Change often is not conceived of as being multidimensional. Objectively, it is possible to clarify the meaning of an educational change by identifying and describing its separate dimensions. Ignorance of these dimensions explains a number of interesting phenomena in the field of educational changes : for example, why some people accept an innovation they do not understand; why some aspects of a change are implemented and others not; why strategies for change neglect certain essential components. The concept of objective reality is tricky. Reality is always defined by individuals and groups. But individuals and groups interact to produce social phenomena (constitutions, laws, policies, educational change programmes), which exist outside any given individual. There is also the danger that the objective reality is only the reflection of the producers of change and thus simply a glorified version of their subjective conceptions.
